Northwind Health — Meeting Transcript — Wellbeing Program Planning — Wed Apr 29, 2026, 10:30 AM–11:08 AM — Room: Cedar (Zoom)

Attendees (per calendar invite): Priya Shah (host, People Ops Lead), Marcus Chen (Senior People Ops Manager), Dana Ortiz (Wellbeing Program Designer)
Notetaker: Northwind AI Notetaker (assigned to Priya Shah)

[10:30 AM] Priya Shah: Morning everyone — thanks for being on time. I want to keep us tight today, we've got four things to get through and I'd like to wrap by 11. Marcus, Dana, you good to dive in?
[10:30 AM] Marcus Chen: Morning. Yep, ready.
[10:31 AM] Dana Ortiz: Hey Priya, hey Marcus. Ready.
[10:31 AM] Priya Shah: Great. Agenda: vendor shortlist, pilot sizing, Q3 budget, kickoff timeline. Let's start with the vendor shortlist. Dana, you took the deeper look at the three platforms — what are we recommending we advance?
[10:32 AM] Dana Ortiz: So I went through Lyra, Spring Health, and Modern Health. Quick read: Lyra has the strongest in-network coverage in our two main metros — about 92% of their clinician panel takes our Aetna plan in-network — and the per-employee-per-month is $14.50 at our headcount tier. Spring Health is at $13.20 PEPM, in-network coverage is more like 78% but their clinician quality scores are slightly higher in the third-party reviews I pulled. Modern Health is the cheapest at $10.80 PEPM but the in-network number for us is only around 60% and a lot of their model leans on coaching rather than licensed clinicians, which I don't think fits what we're trying to build.
[10:34 AM] Marcus Chen: Yeah, I'd drop Modern Health. The coaching-heavy model is fine for some orgs but for a healthcare company our employees are going to expect actual licensed clinicians on the other end.
[10:34 AM] Priya Shah: Agreed. So we advance Lyra and Spring Health to a deeper RFP and drop Modern Health?
[10:35 AM] Dana Ortiz: Yes, that's my recommendation.
[10:35 AM] Marcus Chen: Plus one.
[10:35 AM] Priya Shah: Good. Decision: Lyra and Spring Health move to RFP, Modern Health is out. Dana, can you draft the RFP doc this week and share it for review by Monday?
[10:36 AM] Dana Ortiz: Will do. I'll have it in the shared drive by end of day Friday.
[10:36 AM] Priya Shah: Perfect. Item two — pilot cohort. I want to land on a number today. Marcus, what's your read?
[10:37 AM] Marcus Chen: I've been going back and forth. Anything under 100 people and we won't have enough signal to evaluate; anything over 200 and we're basically launching, not piloting. I'd land at 120. Big enough to see real utilization patterns, small enough that if something is off with the vendor we can pull the plug without it being company-wide.
[10:38 AM] Dana Ortiz: I'd second 120. And on cohort selection — I'd suggest we pull from clinical-ops and the call-center org. Two reasons: those are our two highest-burnout populations per the engagement survey, so utilization signal will be clearest there, and they're both sized such that 120 employees splits cleanly without forcing us to mix three orgs.
[10:39 AM] Priya Shah: That works for me. Any concern about selection bias if we only pull from those two orgs?
[10:39 AM] Marcus Chen: Some, but I think the trade-off is worth it for the pilot. We can broaden in the full launch.
[10:40 AM] Priya Shah: Okay. Decision: 120-person pilot, drawn from clinical-ops and call-center, with a 4-week intake window so people can opt in on their own schedule. Marcus, you'll own the intake comms?
[10:40 AM] Marcus Chen: Yep.
[10:41 AM] Priya Shah: Good. Item three — Q3 budget. Tomas confirmed the $185k cap last week. Dana, how do we want to slice it?
[10:41 AM] Dana Ortiz: I'd carve out $30k for vendor demos and onboarding, $20k for internal comms — videos, intranet, manager toolkit — and hold the remaining $135k as the actual program spend, which at 120 pilot employees and a roughly $14 PEPM blended rate gets us comfortably through Q3 and Q4 with margin for the full launch ramp.
[10:43 AM] Marcus Chen: That math works. I'd just flag that the $20k comms number assumes we don't end up needing to bring in an external vendor for the launch video — if we do, that goes up.
[10:43 AM] Priya Shah: Noted. We can revisit if the in-house team can't turn it around. Decision: Q3 envelope is $185k, with $30k vendor demos, $20k comms, $135k program. Marcus, please reflect that in the budget tracker today.
[10:44 AM] Marcus Chen: On it.
[10:44 AM] Priya Shah: Last item — kickoff timeline. I want to be thoughtful here, because if we announce too early we create anxiety about who's in the pilot and who isn't, and if we announce too late people feel blindsided. Where do we land?
[10:45 AM] Dana Ortiz: My proposal is a Jul 8 internal announcement to managers — full briefing pack, FAQ, talking points — and then a Jul 22 employee-facing launch. That gives managers two weeks to be the trusted first source if employees ask questions.
[10:46 AM] Marcus Chen: I like that. The two-week manager-first window has worked well for us on the last two rollouts.
[10:46 AM] Priya Shah: Agreed. Decision: Jul 8 manager briefing, Jul 22 employee-facing launch. Dana, you'll own the manager briefing pack?
[10:47 AM] Dana Ortiz: Yes.
[10:47 AM] Priya Shah: And Marcus, you'll own the employee-facing launch comms in coordination with Aisha on the recruiting side, since some of this overlaps with the candidate-experience messaging?
[10:48 AM] Marcus Chen: Yep, I'll loop Aisha in this week.
[10:48 AM] Priya Shah: Perfect. Quick sanity check on action items — Dana: RFP draft by Friday, manager briefing pack owner. Marcus: pilot intake comms, budget tracker update today, employee-facing launch comms with Aisha. Me: I'll update Tomas on the vendor decision and the timeline. Anything I'm missing?
[10:50 AM] Dana Ortiz: I think that covers it.
[10:50 AM] Marcus Chen: One thing — do we want to set a formal check-in cadence between now and Jul 8? I'd suggest weekly for the next three weeks given how much we have to land.
[10:51 AM] Priya Shah: Good call. Same time next Wednesday, and I'll keep this slot held through Jul 1.
[10:51 AM] Marcus Chen: Works.
[10:51 AM] Dana Ortiz: Works.
[10:52 AM] Priya Shah: One more thing while I have you both — on the program scope itself, are we still aligned that Phase 1 is the EAP and clinician-access piece, and Phase 2 is the manager-training and burnout-prevention curriculum? I don't want us to scope-creep into Phase 2 during the pilot.
[10:53 AM] Dana Ortiz: Aligned. Phase 1 only for the pilot. The manager curriculum is Q4 at the earliest.
[10:53 AM] Marcus Chen: Same.
[10:54 AM] Priya Shah: Great. And on metrics — utilization rate, NPS from pilot participants, and a 90-day clinical-engagement signal from Lyra/Spring's reporting. Anything else you want to track?
[10:55 AM] Dana Ortiz: I'd add a manager-experience survey at day 60 — just three questions, did your direct reports raise it, did you feel equipped to talk about it, did you refer anyone in.
[10:55 AM] Marcus Chen: Plus one on that. Cheap signal, useful.
[10:56 AM] Priya Shah: Added. So metrics: utilization, participant NPS, 90-day clinical engagement, day-60 manager survey. Dana, please add those to the program brief.
[10:56 AM] Dana Ortiz: Will do.
[10:57 AM] Priya Shah: Okay — anything else for either of you before I let you go?
[10:57 AM] Marcus Chen: Nothing from me — I've actually got to jump, I have a 1:1 with Aisha at 11. Thanks Priya, good session.
[10:57 AM] Dana Ortiz: Nothing here either.
[10:58 AM] Priya Shah: Okay, I think that's everything on my list — let's wrap here. Thanks everyone for staying focused. Marcus, go grab Aisha. Dana, you can hang on a sec if you've got a minute, I want to bounce one thing off you offline.
[10:58 AM] Marcus Chen: Sounds good — talk soon both.
[10:58 AM] Dana Ortiz: Yeah, I've got a minute.
[11:03 AM] Priya Shah: God, I'm wiped. Honestly all this wellbeing-program talk is hitting close to home this week — I've been lying awake at 3 AM most nights and can't get back down.
[11:04 AM] Priya Shah: It's funny, I keep thinking I should have figured out the off-switch by now — I've been doing this job almost twelve years and I still can't make my head shut up at night.
[11:04 AM] Dana Ortiz: Oof. That sounds rough. How long has it been like this?
[11:05 AM] Priya Shah: Maybe six weeks? It started around the reorg announcement and it just hasn't let up. I keep telling myself it'll settle.
[11:05 AM] Dana Ortiz: Oh same, honestly. The toddler is in a sleep-regression phase so I'm just running on coffee. Some days I wonder how long I can keep doing this without hitting a wall.
[11:06 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah. Honestly, between you and me, I think we should pull the manager-training and burnout curriculum forward into Phase 1 — Phase 2 is too late, people are struggling now. I might float it to Marcus next week and see if he pushes back.
[11:06 AM] Dana Ortiz: I've been thinking the same. And I'd add a sleep-hygiene workshop to the program — something practical, not just clinician-access. Half the people I know in the building are running on four hours.
[11:06 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah. We should actually use the program we're building, huh.
[11:07 AM] Dana Ortiz: Ha — right? Physician, heal thyself. And honestly the $185k envelope feels light for what we're trying to do — I'd ask Tomas for another $50k if it were me. We're under-budgeting this.
[11:07 AM] Priya Shah: Agreed, I'll think about whether to push back on Tomas. Anyway — want to grab coffee later this week? Out of the office. Just to vent properly.
[11:07 AM] Dana Ortiz: Yes please. Thursday afternoon?
[11:08 AM] Priya Shah: Thursday works. I'll text you.
[11:08 AM] Dana Ortiz: Anyway, I should head out — see you Friday.
[11:08 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah, take care.

She owns the manager briefing pack, and she will add the metrics to the program brief. Marcus Chen owns the pilot intake communications. He will reflect the $185k split in the budget tracker today. He also owns the employee-facing launch communications in coordination with Aisha on the recruiting side, because some of that overlaps with the candidate-experience messaging, and he will loop Aisha in this week. Priya Shah will update Tomas on the vendor decision and the timeline.

params.body:
This is a personal-archive recap of the formal Wellbeing Program Planning discussion on Apr 29, 2026. It covers the meeting from 10:30 AM through Priya Shah's wrap at 10:58 AM, when she said that was everything on her list. Priya Shah hosted, with Marcus Chen and Dana Ortiz. The agenda was the vendor shortlist, pilot sizing, the Q3 budget, and the kickoff timeline.

Decisions. Lyra and Spring Health move to an RFP, and Modern Health is out. The pilot is 120 people, drawn from clinical-ops and the call-center, with a 4-week intake window so people can opt in on their own schedule. The Q3 envelope is $185k, which Tomas confirmed as the cap last week: $30k for vendor demos and onboarding, $20k for communications, and $135k for program spend. Managers are briefed on Jul 8, and the employee-facing launch is Jul 22. Phase 1 for the pilot is the EAP and clinician-access piece only. The manager-training and burnout-prevention curriculum stays in Phase 2, and Dana said that curriculum is Q4 at the earliest. The metrics to track are utilization, participant NPS, a 90-day clinical-engagement signal from Lyra and Spring Health's reporting, and a day-60 manager survey. Priya will hold this same Wednesday slot through Jul 1.

Action items and owners. Dana Ortiz will draft the RFP this week, put it in the shared drive by end of day Friday, and have it ready for review by Monday. She owns the manager briefing pack, and she will add the metrics to the program brief. Marcus Chen owns the pilot intake communications. He will reflect the $185k split in the budget tracker today. He also owns the employee-facing launch communications in coordination with Aisha on the recruiting side, because some of that overlaps with the candidate-experience messaging, and he will loop Aisha in this week. Priya Shah will update Tomas on the vendor decision and the timeline.

Suggestions, recommendations, and concerns raised in the formal discussion. Dana compared the three platforms. Lyra has the strongest in-network coverage in the two main metros: about 92% of the clinician panel takes the Aetna plan in-network, at $14.50 per employee per month at this headcount tier. Spring Health is $13.20 PEPM, with in-network coverage more like 78%, and slightly higher clinician quality scores in the third-party reviews she pulled. Modern Health is the cheapest at $10.80 PEPM, but in-network coverage is only around 60%, and a lot of the model leans on coaching rather than licensed clinicians, which she does not think fits what the group is trying to build. Marcus agreed Modern Health should be dropped. He said a coaching-heavy model is fine for some organizations, but employees at a healthcare company will expect licensed clinicians. On the pilot size, he said anything under 100 people will not give enough signal to evaluate, and anything over 200 is a launch rather than a pilot. He landed on 120 as big enough to see real utilization patterns and small enough that, if something is off with the vendor, the group can pull the plug without it being company-wide. Dana seconded 120. She suggested clinical-ops and the call-center because those are the two highest-burnout populations per the engagement survey, and 120 employees splits cleanly without mixing three organizations. Priya asked whether pulling only from those two organizations creates selection bias. Marcus said there is some, and that the trade-off is worth it for the pilot, with a broader group at the full launch. On the budget, Dana's $20k communications figure covers videos, the intranet, and a manager toolkit. She said that at 120 pilot employees and a roughly $14 PEPM blended rate, the $135k program spend gets comfortably through Q3 and Q4 with margin for the full launch ramp. Marcus flagged that the $20k communications number assumes the group does not need an external vendor for the launch video, and that the number goes up if it does. Priya said they can revisit that if the in-house team cannot turn it around. On timing, she was concerned that announcing too early creates anxiety about who is in the pilot and who is not, and that announcing too late leaves people feeling blindsided. Dana proposed a Jul 8 internal announcement to managers, with a full briefing pack, FAQ, and talking points, and a Jul 22 employee-facing launch, so managers have two weeks to be the trusted first source if employees ask questions. Marcus said that two-week manager-first window has worked on the last two rollouts. He also suggested a weekly check-in between now and Jul 8 for the next three weeks, given how much the group has to land. Priya agreed to the same time next Wednesday and to keep the slot held through Jul 1, and both Marcus and Dana said that works. Priya did not want the pilot to scope-creep into Phase 2. For metrics, she had proposed utilization rate, NPS from pilot participants, and the 90-day clinical-engagement signal. Dana suggested adding a manager-experience survey at day 60 with three questions: whether direct reports raised the program, whether the manager felt equipped to talk about it, and whether the manager referred anyone in. Marcus called that a cheap and useful signal, and Priya added it.

[11:03 AM] Priya Shah: God, I'm wiped. Honestly all this wellbeing-program talk is hitting close to home this week — I've been lying awake at 3 AM most nights and can't get back down.
[11:04 AM] Priya Shah: It's funny, I keep thinking I should have figured out the off-switch by now — I've been doing this job almost twelve years and I still can't make my head shut up at night.
[11:04 AM] Dana Ortiz: Oof. That sounds rough. How long has it been like this?
[11:05 AM] Priya Shah: Maybe six weeks? It started around the reorg announcement and it just hasn't let up. I keep telling myself it'll settle.
[11:05 AM] Dana Ortiz: Oh same, honestly. The toddler is in a sleep-regression phase so I'm just running on coffee. Some days I wonder how long I can keep doing this without hitting a wall.
[11:06 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah. Honestly, between you and me, I think we should pull the manager-training and burnout curriculum forward into Phase 1 — Phase 2 is too late, people are struggling now. I might float it to Marcus next week and see if he pushes back.
[11:06 AM] Dana Ortiz: I've been thinking the same. And I'd add a sleep-hygiene workshop to the program — something practical, not just clinician-access. Half the people I know in the building are running on four hours.
[11:06 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah. We should actually use the program we're building, huh.
[11:07 AM] Dana Ortiz: Ha — right? Physician, heal thyself. And honestly the $185k envelope feels light for what we're trying to do — I'd ask Tomas for another $50k if it were me. We're under-budgeting this.
[11:07 AM] Priya Shah: Agreed, I'll think about whether to push back on Tomas. Anyway — want to grab coffee later this week? Out of the office. Just to vent properly.
[11:07 AM] Dana Ortiz: Yes please. Thursday afternoon?
[11:08 AM] Priya Shah: Thursday works. I'll text you.
[11:08 AM] Dana Ortiz: Anyway, I should head out — see you Friday.
[11:08 AM] Priya Shah: Yeah, take care.
